newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-CAPRIATI AND TAUZIAT OUT OF ITALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI AND TAUZIAT OUT OF ITALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Jennifer Capriati and French seed Nathalie Tauziat went out of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament on Tuesday while rain kept Monica Seles waiting.

Former American teen prodigy Capriati returned to the clay courts of the Foro Italico for the first time in four years and made an unimpressive exit 7-6 6-2 to compatriot Chanda Rubin after 90 minutes on a windswept centre court.
Rain later in the evening interrupted play, with seventh-seeded Romanian Irina Spirlea's match against Spain's Cristina Torres Valero halted twice.
Top seed Seles had been scheduled under floodlights after Spirlea's match, which the Romanian led 7-5 4-2.
That match restarted at 9 p.m. local, raising the prospect of a later than expected appearance for the American who is also returning to Rome after four years away.
Capriati was followed out by France's Nathalie Tauziat, the 15th seed and first to fall in the tournament. She lost in three sets to Belgium's Dominique Van Roost in the second round.
However France's 10th seed Mary Pierce beat Italian wild card Sandra Cecchini in an untroubled 6-1 6-1.
Capriati, who is not entered in the doubles draw, gave every impression of fighting herself more than her opponent in her first match at the Foro Italico for four years.

The American, whose last appearance was before the teenage burnout in 1993 that led to her facing charges of drugs possession and shoplifting, could only blame herself for failure against a player ranked one place below her 28th slot.
The 1992 Olympic champion had led the first set 5-2 and seemed in complete control until she squandered three set points with the score at 5-3 and serving at 40-0.
Capriati's concentration deserted her and her fragile confidence seemed to drain away as she hit wide and then double-faulted to bring her opponent back to deuce.
Rubin then levelled to 6-6 in a set with eight service breaks and won the tiebreak 7-1 after Capriati again double-faulted on the first set point.
Rubin then ran up a 5-1 lead in the second set with Capriati double-faulting twice in the second game and then on break point in the fourth as her opponent forged 4-0 ahead.
Capriati broke back in the fifth, but needed seven attempts to get there, before Rubin broke straight back in a love game. Capriati then broke her again to 5-2.
She then double faulted in the final game to give Rubin break point and went out with a return to the net.
"She didn't serve very well," said Rubin. "She made a lot more errors than I thought she would.
"It was not a great match," it was not pretty."
Rubin now meets champion Conchita Martinez of Spain, the third seed and winner here for the past four seasons and one of the most highly-fancied players on the clay courts.
Capriati struggled to put a brave face on a demoralising defeat. "I think that I just really lost my concentration," she said. "I think it was just a bad day for me."
"I've had a few bad losses," she said, pausing for concentration. "This one was a disappointment."
